Both the Python Stop-hooks (via _lexicon.py) and the TS runtime (slidePostProcessor / wikiService, migrating) import THIS file; the prose twin anti-slop-lexicon.md is the human-readable + manifest-retrieved version. A drift guard (scripts/lexicon-drift-guard.py) warns if the two diverge. Do not add a banned term to a hook or a skill inline - add it here.

tier1_always._rule: Field guide Rule 1 - hard-flag on sight, any single occurrence. Replace with the plain equivalent.

tier2_cluster._rule: Field guide Rule 2 - fine in isolation, flagged only when TWO OR MORE appear in the same paragraph (or one slide). Do not hard-ban these; cluster-gate them.

openers_banned._rule: Rules 3-6, 9, 29 - fire only at sentence/bullet/paragraph START.

closers_banned._rule: Rules 5, 8 - grandiose conclusion fillers + engagement closers.
phrases: at the end of the day
when all is said and done

multiword_banned._rule: Rule 10, 11 - token-sequence slop + GPTZero high-multiplier phrases.

structural_regex._rule: Rule 23-34, 94.4 - the highest-signal STRUCTURAL tells. JS/Python compatible source strings; weight 3x a single word hit (Rule 95).
structural_regex.negative_parallelism: (?i)\b(it'?s not (just |only )?\w[\w ]{0,40}?,? it'?s\b|not just \w[\w ]{0,40}? but\b|isn'?t about \w[\w ]{0,40}? it'?s about\b|more than just\b|goes beyond\b)
structural_regex.stacked_hedging: (?i)\b(could potentially|may,? in some (cases|circumstances),? possibly|generally speaking, in many cases)\b

positive_voice._rule: Pillar 4 - what GOOD prose does. These are PRESCRIPTIONS for the human-voice-editor skill + generation, not bans.
rules: Lead with the answer (BLUF); the first sentence states the finding.
Active voice with a named actor.
Omit needless words (in order to->to, the fact that->cut, a number of->some).
Anchor every claim to a name, place, mechanism, or concrete instance (a figure is one anchor among several, only inside a cited quote).
Vary cadence: mix short and long sentences; never three same-shape sentences or three same-opener sentences/bullets in a row.
Take a position; at most one qualifier per claim.
Trust the reader; cut throat-clearing and self-structure narration.
Reuse the precise domain term verbatim; no elegant variation.
Contractions allowed and preferred in conversational chat replies.
Override (Orwell rule 6): break any rule sooner than write something barbarous; log the exception.

title_contestability._rule: Rules 14/43-47/58 + HiC Quantitative Claim Rule. A headline/theme-name earns its place by being SPECIFIC and CONTESTABLE, never by carrying a figure.
title_contestability.require: a verb / claim someone could disagree with; not a topic label; not a platitude; a figure does NOT satisfy.
